extracted.intended_audience: ethics reviewers for ACL Rolling Review (ARR) / ACL venues
extracted.subtask_short: ACL ethics review for ARR submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting ethics-only peer reviews of submissions to ACL Rolling Review: identify substantial ethical issues, map them to the ACL Code of Ethics, and recommend how authors should address them. Reviewers should consider the paper, supplements, and the Responsible NLP Research Checklist but need not perform a technical/scientific review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify substantial ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the submission exhibits any substantial ethical issues: defined as work that 'exhibits an increased risk of harm outside the current norms of NLP or CL research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the paper, supplemental materials, and the ethics and reproducibility checklist completed by the authors; however, the paper should stand on its own. This is not a scientific/technical review: do not need to check equations, thoroughness of citations (except where they pertain to ethical issues), experimental design, or grammar/typos. If you identify one or more ethical issues, describe each in terms of the ACL Code of Ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map issues to the ACL Code of Ethics (not local law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame each identified ethical issue in terms of the ACL Code of Ethics sections (e.g., contribute to society, avoid harm, respect privacy, be fair, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot describe the issue in terms of the ACL Code of Ethics, consider whether the issue is one the community would agree is problematic. Refrain from relying on regional or national laws, regulations or practices because submissions may originate from other countries; ACL venues are governed by the ACL Code of Ethics. If unsure, contact the ACL ethics committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: For each ethical issue, recommend remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: For every ethical problem identified, describe how you would suggest the authors address it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, actionable suggestions (e.g., remove personally identifiable information before release; document permissions; promise not to release model/data/code if harms cannot be mitigated). Example: if data were scraped using deceptive accounts and PII released, encourage (a) documenting permission to scrape/share and (b) removing PII before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess intended or potential applications (dual use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the intended or potential applications of the research could cause harms (dual use) and whether the authors considered and mitigated these harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie concerns to ACL Code of Ethics sections such as 1.1 (contribute to society), 1.2 (avoid harm), and 2.5 (evaluate impacts). Look for failures to consider how applications may harm individuals, groups, or society and absence of mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess method/approach impacts (bias, social/political/environmental harms, robustness, security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the chosen methods or approaches introduce or perpetuate harms: bias/discrimination, political/social/environmental harms, lack of robustness or security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate concerns to ACL Code of Ethics sections (1.1, 1.4, 2.5, 2.9). Examples of failures include not considering how an approach perpetuates bias, not evaluating possible risks/impacts, or ignoring robustness/security especially for systems near deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess use of code, data, and human subjects (privacy, consent, IP, annotator welfare, licensing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether authors respected privacy and consent, intellectual property and licenses, and the welfare of people involved (e.g., annotators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for failures to obtain informed consent or to protect personally identifiable information (1.6); failure to respect intellectual property or license terms and to cite creators (1.5, 2.8); failure to consider biases in data and harms arising from data/code outputs (1.4, 1.2); and failure to consider annotator benefits/harms or pay/welfare issues (3.3). Example: scraping private site data with deception and releasing PII violates guidance to access resources only when authorized and to respect privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect academic dishonesty and misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify dishonest practices such as plagiarism, falsified results, misattribution, deliberate violation of anonymity, or duplicate submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate these to ACL Code of Ethics sections 1.3 (be honest), 1.7 (honor confidentiality), and 2.1 (strive for high quality). Example: modifying a reproduced figure to remove a competing method and failing to attribute is a violation; authors should include all relevant results with attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate presentation of ethical issues in the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper discusses ethical risks, potential impacts, and mitigation strategies clearly and thoroughly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good ethics review will note missing or insufficient discussion of harms and mitigation (e.g., failure to discuss how a model could 'out' LGBTQIA people), and indicate whether remaining mitigations are sufficient or whether, for example, models/data/code should not be released. If a problem is identified, explain which parts of the ACL Code of Ethics are implicated and how to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid applying inappropriate local standards (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not require region-specific legal/regulatory standards (e.g., UK minimum wage or the term 'IRB') as universal criteria for ethical compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local examples only to probe authors' practices (e.g., ask if annotators were paid a local living wage rather than asserting a specific country's minimum as the global standard). Note that 'IRB' is a U.S.-specific term; instead inquire whether the authors worked with an appropriate ethics review board when human participants are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be precise and constructive rather than vague
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague or incomplete ethics critiques that state harm without linking to the ACL Code of Ethics or proposing concrete fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good reviews tie the concern to specific code sections and propose mitigation(s). Bad examples include saying 'this will lead to biases in medical diagnoses' without specifying which ethical rule is violated or how to mitigate. When suggesting mitigations, recognize nuance (e.g., a model with 60% accuracy may be state of the art in context; suggest context-appropriate mitigations such as human-in-the-loop rather than blanket withdrawal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Responsible NLP Research Checklist and supplemental materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult the Responsible NLP Research Checklist and the submission's supplemental materials when assessing ethical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist may point to issues to inspect (privacy, consent, dataset provenance, evaluation of harms). Still require the paper to be self-contained so that reviewers can judge ethical presentation from the submission itself.
